newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress says ready for talks with rulers.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress says ready for talks with rulers.

text.p: The head of India's Congress party, Sitaram Kesri, said on Tuesday that he was ready to hold talks with the United Front coalition provided the ruling alliance came forward with a proposal.
"I am ready for talks if the proposal comes from their side. There is no doubt in it," Kesri told Reuters after addressing a political rally in the Indian capital.

Earlier on Tuesday, Kesri had been quoted as saying talks could begin provided Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda stepped down. But the Congress leader made no mention of such a precondition either to Reuters or at the rally.
"We are hungry for respect, not for power," Kesri told party supporters at the rally.
"This is a fight not of personalities, but of principles. I don't have anything personal against Deve Gowda," he said.

Kesri triggered a political crisis on March 30 when he announced the withdrawal of Congress's vital support to Deve Gowda's minority government. Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence in parliament on Friday.
